chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
The one who dies and has no inheritor from his relatives, nor a master who freed him and assumed responsibility for his crimes, then his wealth is from the spoils (public treasury).

key_terms.مَوْلَى عَتَاقِهِ: Master who freed him (and assumed responsibility)

ai.seo_question: What happens to the wealth of a person who dies with no heirs in Shia Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the inheritance distribution for an individual lacking both blood relatives (qaraba) and a patron (mawla), a scenario central to Shia jurisprudence regarding the scope of the public treasury. It establishes that such wealth is classified as 'anfal' (gains), signifying its direct transfer to the Imam or the state treasury rather than being distributed among specific heirs. This ruling underscores the comprehensive nature of the Bayt al-Mal in managing assets of those without familial or contractual ties.
